market_impact_summary.en: No significant changes in traditional markets today as they are closed for the weekend. The last close showed a positive sentiment with S&P 500 up and VIX down.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso con risultati misti: il Nikkei in rialzo dello 0.28%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.43% e l'Hang Seng in perdita dell'1.59%.

Mentre i mercati tradizionali sono chiusi per il fine settimana, riepiloghiamo la chiusura precedente. L'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dell'1.08%, il VIX in calo dell'11.06% e il Dollar Index sostanzialmente invariato. L'oro ha perso l'1.21%, il petrolio ha guadagnato lo 0.93%.

Sul fronte macro, nessun dato rilevante in uscita oggi. La Global M2 Liquidity continua ad espandersi, con un aumento del 4.7% su base annua.

Tra le notizie, l'accordo sull'Iran non sembra dare sollievo ai timori sull'inflazione delle banche centrali. In Asia, le preoccupazioni geopolitiche continuano a influenzare le catene di approvvigionamento, in particolare per il Giappone.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i sessantamila dollari, con una variazione positiva dell'1,16% a 63.418 dollari. Tuttavia, i flussi ETF mostrano un deflusso di 90,7 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle probabilità di un aumento dei tassi della Fed a luglio, che si attestano intorno al 40%.

Per quanto riguarda le altcoin, Ethereum guadagna l'1,48% a mille settecentoventidue dollari, mentre Solana registra un aumento del 4,22% a settantuno virgola quarantatré dollari. Anche BNB mostra un incremento del 2,07% a cinquecentottantacinque virgola novantaquattro dollari.

Il Fear & Greed Index è a 23, in territorio di Extreme Fear, il che suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. Asian markets closed with mixed results: Nikkei up 0.28%, Shanghai down 0.43%, and Hang Seng down 1.59%. While traditional markets are closed for the weekend, let's recap the previous close. The S&P 500 closed up 1.08%, VIX down 11.06%, and the Dollar Index essentially flat. Gold lost 1.21%, and oil gained 0.93%. On the macro front, no significant data releases today. The Global M2 Liquidity continues to expand, up 4.7% year-over-year. Among the news, the Iran agreement doesn't seem to alleviate central banks' inflation fears. In Asia, geopolitical concerns continue to impact supply chains, particularly in Japan. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin holds above sixty thousand dollars, up 1.16% at $63,418 However, ETF flows show an outflow of $90.7 million. This move could be influenced by the 40% probability of a Fed rate hike in July. Regarding altcoins, Ethereum gains 1.48% at $1,722, while Solana rises 4.22% at $71.43 BNB also shows a 2.07% increase at $585.94 The Fear & Greed Index is at 23, in Extreme Fear territory, suggesting investor caution. No macro data on the agenda today. For a deeper dive into today's topics, find the full articles on our platform in the Top Stories section. Thanks for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Stablecoin remuneration on centralised exchanges
articles.snippet: by Wenqian Huang, Nikola Tarashev, Xinyi Wang Centralised exchanges remunerate stablecoin holders, using the return on the issuer's reserve assets or income from market activity. Under the reserve-based model, yields track policy rates – akin to yields on cash-management instruments – whereas under the activity-based model, yields are much more volatile. By turning stablecoins into substitutes for bank deposits or money market funds or into funding instruments for exchanges' risky activities, remuneration models may shape the macro financial implications of wide stablecoin adoption in the future.

articles.snippet: Rising geopolitical tensions and increasing fragmentation introduce new risks into global production networks, forcing both disruptions and creating new strategic opportunities. The shortages follow repeated attacks on refineries and fuel infrastructure that have steadily chipped away at Russia's refining system.
